scenario: IRET.10.7 / LGRA.10.1.4: `withdraw j` in an `after` body removes the matched Job when the timer fires. The body logs "timer" and then withdraws `j`, and `gone` fires once no Job is left: ["armed 1", "timer", "gone 1"]. A withdraw at fire time gives ["armed 1", "gone 1", "timer"]. PATH PINNED: the `after` clause's capture fact carrying `j` as a reference (`dsc.rete` `action_captures`), and ACTION_WITHDRAW_BY_ID on the follow-up rule's terminal (`rete/engine.c`). Its by-identity form runs on both runtimes as the Mercury differential scenario 89_withdraw_nested.
rules_ds:
schema Anchor scope explicit:
    v: Int

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    log info "armed {j.id}"
    after 5_s:
        log info "timer"
        withdraw j

rule gone:
    Anchor a
    no Job
->
    log info "gone {a.v}"
